full_judgment:
2. In a suit for eviction of the defendants from the suit premises, SCC Suit No.1 bf 1983 of the Second Court of Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Serajgonj, a decree was passed not at the first instance but upon review under Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In revision before the High Court Division against the said decree the defendants raised the only question that a review does not lie in a proceeding under the Small Cause Courts Act, 1887. A Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 3rd July, 1997, upon a comprehensive review of the legal position clearly found that the Small Cause Courts have jurisdiction to entertain and decide a review application. It was held: 

 4. Mr Karim has made the submission with reference to clause (c) of section 114 of the Code of Civil Procedure the purport of which is that a review would lie from "a decision on a reference from a Court of Small Causes". Now section 113 CPC provides that any Court may refer a case for the opinion of the High Court Division and the High Court Division may make such order thereon as it thinks fit. So, what clause (c) of section 114 provides is that, if there is a decision on a reference from a Court of Small Causes, obviously it will be a decision of the High Court Division, a review would lie or the said decision. Review from a decree or order of a Court of Small Causes will be maintainable not under clause (c) but under clauses (a) and (b) of section 114 read with Order 47 rule 1 CPC.
